newsitem.title: THAILAND: RESEARCH ALERT - Thai banks to grow 6.3 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Thai banks to grow 6.3 pct in 1997.

text.p: Profit growth in the Thai banking sector in 1997, excluding the performance of Bangkok Bank of Commerce Plc, will average 6.3 percent, Jardine Fleming Thanakom Securities said on Friday.

Including the performance of Bangkok Bank of Commerce, which is struggling with under 85 billion baht of non-performing loans, brings the sector growth projection to a negative 0.2 percent in 1997, banking analyst Scott Christensen told Reuters.

Thailand's four largest banks, Bangkok Bank, Krung Thai Bank, Thai Farmers Bank and Siam Commerical Bank were generally better prepared than the rest to withstand a deteriorating operating environment brought on by a slowdown in the Thai economy, Christensen said.

"We expect the top four banks to post profit growth in the range of five to eight percent and we are confident that most of them have sufficient excess loan-loss reserves to cover expected increases in non-performing loans," he said.
The central bank on Thursday said the Thai economy was expected to grow by around 7.0 percent year-on-year in 1996, its lowest level for a decade.
Jardine Fleming said it expects bank sectoral income growth to average 8.3 percent for 1996, declining to 3.5 percent if Bangkok Bank of Commerce's performance is included.
Concerns about a possible deterioration in loan portfolio quality in 1997, as the Thai economic growth slows, primarily surrounded selected second tier and smaller banks, it said.
"Our concern focuses on most of the rest of the sector where profit growth could slow down more dramatically," Christensen said.

The Thai banks, excluding Bangkok Bank of Commmerce, have averaged earnings growth of 12 percent in the first nine months of this year, compared with nearly 15 percent in the corresponding period in 1995, according to calculations by Thai Farmers Bank Research Centre.
